# 3,002 less-committed Claude Code statuslines, one section each

Every project with 10 to 44 commits (the 20-44 band opens with six tied at 45 that fell just outside the top 1,000), the 2-9 commit projects with at least 200 lines of statusline code that are not mostly a copy of one already read, and the 0-1 commit projects with at least 400 such lines. Ranks continue from [projects.md](projects.md) over every eligible project, so gaps are the projects not read. Sections were written by haiku agents from the downloaded source on 2026-10-26. Selection and fields: [README.md](README.md).

## 20-44 commits

### 1001. limone-eth/terminally.social
45 commits (0 in the last 90 days), 3 stars, last commit 2026-06-15
- url: https://github.com/limone-eth/terminally.social
- what: statusline inside a larger tool (terminally.social, a friends' daily token-burn leaderboard with a public server; the statusline draws its friends feed)
- size: ~106 code lines, JavaScript (client/statusline.js, 143 lines total)
- shape: rich
- data sources: stdin, network
- lineage: wraps or configures X (wraps whatever base_statusline command the user configures, run via bash -c at client/statusline.js:116; claude-hud appears only as the example in its header comment)
- why it exists: a token-burn leaderboard among friends, published as a product on a public server
- beyond baseline: friends feed appended under the base line, ranked working/idle/offline and capped at four (client/statusline.js:54); render from cache only, with a detached `presence.js pull` started when the cache is older than 30s and throttled by a 5s lock file (client/statusline.js:22, :87); per-session token totals are summed from transcript usage by the hook, not by the statusline (client/hook.js:22-36)
- summary: Renders the user's own statusline first, falling back to a built-in `[model] dir` line, then appends one line of friends' presence read from a local cache file. Statusline rendering never does network I/O: when the cache is stale it spawns a detached `presence.js pull` that refreshes it for the next tick, with a lock file so only one pull runs per few seconds. The statusline itself only reads the cache; the transcript is read by the hook, which sums input, output and cache tokens for the session and posts them to the server (client/hook.js:22-36, :78-80). Every section sits in its own try/catch and the script always exits 0, so the code can only add a line.

- beyond baseline: 5-hour block cost bar against a configured cost limit, with a burn-rate projection separator (src/statusline.sh:448-546); daily tracker against the official weekly reset date, with end-of-day projection (src/statusline.sh:742-861); weekly "recommend" mode that turns the weekly remainder into a daily budget (src/statusline.sh:866-930); ccusage_r weekly scheme summing cost on the official reset schedule (src/statusline-utils.sh:175); baseline-offset calibration with tools/calibrate_weekly_usage.sh; context tokens split into cached and fresh from the transcript tail (src/statusline.sh:615-708); tokens-per-minute burn rate (src/statusline.sh:594); countdown to block reset with local reset clock (src/statusline.sh:551-589); monthly total from billing-cycle start (src/statusline-utils.sh:400); active-session counter from recently modified transcripts (src/statusline.sh ~978); dependency-tracked caches (src/statusline-cache.sh:142)
- summary: Runs `npx ccusage blocks` and `ccusage weekly` with --offline to get the active 5-hour block and the weekly cost, then draws each as a two- or three-layer bar whose colour changes at configured multiples of the limit. The projected end-of-window cost is extrapolated from the burn rate (cost + cost/hour x remaining minutes) and drawn as a separator in the bar. The daily figure comes from ccusage blocks filtered to the official reset period, and recommend mode derives a per-day budget from what is left of the weekly limit at the start of the current daily cycle. Context usage is read with awk from the last assistant message in the transcript, separating cache tokens from fresh input. Caches are invalidated when the weekly limit or baseline changes, and the config is validated with jq on every run.

The sample log is what makes the forecast possible, so a fresh install shows no ETA until samples exist.

If the fork is not possible it falls back to a visible ping, after checking that the conversation and the ping fit in the window (hooks/register.tsx:79-85, 321-355). ### 2572. JuDaXia/claude-speed
12 commits (2 in the last 90 days), 2 stars, last commit 2026-08-09
- url: https://github.com/JuDaXia/claude-speed
- what: statusline inside a larger tool (a macOS menu-bar speed monitor and a transcript collector; the statusline is its terminal surface)
- size: ~220 code lines, Python (statusline-speed.py; collect.py adds ~1,100 lines for the menu-bar data)
- shape: rich
- data sources: stdin, transcript, other:subagent transcripts
- lineage: none found
- why it exists: to separate a model's true tokens-per-second from first-token latency, because the author says the feel of speed mostly comes from the fixed first-token cost (README "Why")
- beyond baseline: true tokens per second and first-token latency from a Theil-Sen fit of response duration against output tokens (statusline-speed.py fit_speed, ts_slope); a sliding window that widens until the fit has enough samples (windowed_fit); API error count over the last 30 minutes (response_groups, ERR_ROW_WINDOW); cache hit ratio with a cold flag from the last response (main); background subagent count and fleet tokens per second (agent_metrics)
- summary: The statusline reads the transcript tail and groups consecutive assistant records that share a message ID into one API response, using the time from the previous record as its duration (response_groups). It fits duration against output tokens with a Theil-Sen regression, so the slope gives generation speed and the intercept gives first-token latency, and it widens the window when recent samples are too few (fit_speed, windowed_fit). It also reports the cache hit ratio of the last response, the count of recent API errors, and the fleet burn rate of any running subagents (agent_metrics). The collector in collect.py uses the same parsing to feed the menu-bar app.

The transcript's mtime is taken as the last cache renewal, so the lapse is that time plus the TTL (cache_expiry). The lapse is shown as an absolute clock time, not a countdown, because the line only repaints on conversation events. The next request is priced from the table: a cache read before the lapse, a cache write at 1.25x or 2x after it (PRICES, cache_segment).

Burn rate is the least-squares slope of token use over up to 40 samples per session, kept in the temp dir, and the ETA is remaining headroom divided by that slope (statusline/burnrate.js). Cost is recomputed from transcript usage when statusline-pricing.json has model rates, with streamed duplicate lines removed by message.id, and otherwise scaled from the payload cost (statusline/render.js resolveCost). The PR badge and worktree placement come from stdin.

The five 1.x forks it overlaps (ding113/ccline-packycc, Cubence-com/CubenceLine, hollegjx/uucode, lion231226/glmcode, francismiko/CCometixLine) each credit Haleclipse as their origin and share a pre-2.0 module layout, so the shared code most likely comes from Haleclipse's 1.x base; the overlap does not show that this project copied from any one of them
- why it exists: to show whether Claude's API path is slow or failing and which stage is responsible, alongside git, usage and a themed bar (README)
- beyond baseline: network probes of the Anthropic API using the user's credentials, timing DNS, TCP, TLS and time to first byte, with P95 computed over 12 collected totals and a green, yellow or red health state (src/core/network/network_segment.rs, http_monitor.rs); OAuth masquerade mode that sends the probe as a first-party client (oauth_masquerade.rs); aggregation of errors from Claude Code's JSONL logs (jsonl_monitor.rs); probes triggered by statusline invocations within time windows, with no background process (network_segment.rs header; README); GitHub release update check and geo lookup (src/updater)
- summary: A Rust statusline with git, usage from the transcript, themes and an optional TUI configurator. Its distinctive part is a network monitor that sends a real request to the API on statusline invocations and reports the timing of each stage, so a user can see whether slowness is DNS, TLS or the server. Because the probes ride on statusline invocations, an idle session does not refresh them. The code is a rework of Haleclipse's CCometixLine, and the shared layout with the other 1.x forks is inherited from that base.
